text.text_excerpt: If you want a taste of New Orleans in an afternoon, then you will definitely want to take this tour. We had Linda as our tour guide, and were very happy with all of the information of the city that she gave us as we walked from each location. My two favorite stops on this tour were the Old Coffee Pot Restaurant, and Johnny's Po Boys. These places had the best gumbo and Po'boys that I had during my stay. Make sure you come to this tour hungry, as you will eat a lot. If you have any dietary restrictions, MAKE sure you tell them before you start your tour (I suggest calling them ahead of time). This is a great way to get acquainted with the restaurants and history of the French Quarter. Dave Thomas was our guide and he couldn't have been more personable. There were 15 people on our tour. We never felt crowded, and it was nice to have the opportunity to sit with different people at each stop. The assortment of food was delicious and I cannot comprehend how anyone could be hungry afterward. Ideally this tour should be taken on your 1st day in New Orleans so that you have time to revisit all of the venues.

As others have stated this is a nice walking tour that weaves in and out of air conditioned hotels. Laurie was our guide, knowledgeable, very proud of her heritage and a totally different spin on NOLA than our other tours. Having been to New Orleans on numerous occasions there is always one more restaurant to try. Small group, manageable to get in and out of the establishments, sincerely hot and covered areas to be seated in were limited, cold water provided at each stop. The heaviest portion of the tour was the 1st stop. The muffaletta was of Texas proportion, the po boy had mayo and was not our fave, but eating it on the river front was a nice breeze.
